title: Stamp 2: Laicite
welcome_lead: Stamp the principle of laicite, France's distinctive secularism.
meta_desc: A-Level French adventure on laicite, the 1905 law, and religion in the public sphere.

concepts.def: French principle of separating religion from the public sphere and state institutions.
Law separating Church and State, foundation of French secularism.
Islamic veil, central to debates on religious symbols in schools and public services.
Law banning ostentatious religious symbols in state schools.
Law banning full-face veils (burqa, niqab) in public spaces.
Neutrality required of state institutions and civil servants in religious matters.

walkthroughs.body_html: The 1905 law, passed under Aristide Briand, ended Catholic Church privileges. The state recognises no religion but guarantees freedom of conscience. This frames all later debates.

Three girls were excluded from a Creil school in 1989 for wearing headscarves. The 2004 law eventually banned conspicuous religious symbols in state schools, affecting hijabs, large crosses, and yarmulkes.
Laicite governs the public sphere; private religious practice is protected. Critics argue the principle has been weaponised against Muslim communities; defenders see it as a guarantee of equality.
